dedupe_keys.name: papua new guinea 2018 highlands earthquake building damage and operating status of about 940 health facilities power water infection control as of 28 may 2018

description: This table records how health facilities in Papua New Guinea's Highlands were damaged by the February 2018 earthquake and whether they were still working weeks later. It was compiled by the United Nations in Papua New Guinea from assessments by the World Health Organization, the National Department of Health, the International Committee of the Red Cross, the Australian aid programme (DFAT) and its contractor Cardno. For about 940 facilities in the affected provinces it gives the province, district, name, type, building damage level, assessing agency, coordinates, ownership (government, church or other), whether the facility was open or closed and when, and whether power, water supply and infection control were functioning, with comments on needs, staff and access. Coverage is the earthquake-affected Highlands provinces up to 28 May 2018. The file is free and available to download as Excel under CC BY. Caveats: assessments used different methods and dates, damage levels are qualitative, and many rows are incomplete or awaiting verification. Simulation uses: calibrating fragility and functionality loss of rural health facilities in earthquakes, validating recovery models of health service continuity, and studying the role of power and water in keeping facilities open. Related records: the Türkiye 2023 earthquake health facility damage study (case_study-turkey-2023-earthquake-health-facility-damage) and Healthsites.io (data-healthsites-io).
